## Signatory (Si)

`person` (Employee), `signingTitle`, `signatureAuthority` (Amount with Currency — the ceiling), `contractTypes` (which kinds they may sign; empty = all), `specimenUrl`, `isActive`.

### The authority contract

`canSign(value, contractType) → { allowed, reason }`. Refuses when inactive, when the contract type is outside `contractTypes`, when no ceiling is set, or when `value` exceeds the ceiling — and always says why, so a blocked ceremony tells the user who to route to instead of just stopping. Both arguments are supplied by the caller rather than read off a linked Contract because the check must run before anything is sent, including on a contract not yet created.

Consumed by `verifyCeremony` (signature-block-field) and therefore by Request Signature (before a line goes out), Verify Signature (audit) and Execute Contract (immediately before writing `signed`). Authority is always re-checked from the current card — a signatory deactivated mid-ceremony fails execution even though the request passed.

### Formats

isolated (authority as the hero figure, scope, specimen), embedded, atom, fitted (attribute-only).

### Example

Priya Nair — General Counsel, $250,000 ceiling, vendor/NDA/partnership; signs line 2 of the Acme MSA.

### Non-goals

Not a Legal Entity (the party) and not a Signature Block (the line on the page). No delegation chains — a deputy is a second Signatory card.
